layout: armorClasses lists defender AC columns from 10 down to −10. Each row lists an attacker-level band; targets[i] belongs to armorClasses[i].

matrices.title: Original attack matrix: fighters, paladins, rangers, and related attackers
notes: All 210 cells of matrix I.B were checked against the supplied revised December 1979 Dungeon Masters Guide scan.
The table applies to fighters, paladins, and rangers. Bards use their highest attained fighter level, not their current bard level. Its separate level-0 column applies to halflings and humans.

A cell is the table's 20-sided-die target for the named attacker level band and opponent armor class, before resolving applicable adjustments. It is not automatically equivalent to AC-zero target minus armor class.
The original table repeats 20 in some columns, so a single linear THAC0 subtraction can disagree with it. The examples below use only cells actually legible in this scan.
Any current group convention using simple THAC0 remains a group choice; this reference does not silently replace that convention or the printed matrix.

ruleNotes.title: Missile range adjustments
ruleNotes.text: The matrix prints a −2 adjustment at medium missile range and −5 at long range.

ruleNotes.title: Optional per-level fighter progression
ruleNotes.text: The DM may choose a +1 to-hit bonus at the second level within each two-level fighter band, producing the source's optional per-level progression instead of the ordinary two-level steps. Do not silently apply this option.

ruleNotes.title: Certain spell adjustments change AC
ruleNotes.text: For the listed kinds of spell effects, including curse, prayer, and protection from evil, the DMG instructs the referee to adjust the relevant armor class rather than reduce the attack die result. This preserves the intended repeated-20 behavior. This note is about those spell adjustments, not a universal conversion of every modifier into AC.

ruleNotes.title: Repeated 20s and a separate natural-20 option
ruleNotes.text: The DMG explains the repeated 20s as part of the printed combat-table progression. It then offers an optional amendment: second and later repeated-20 entries require a natural 20, and targets above 20 require a natural 20 plus sufficient bonus. The initial 20 entry still permits die result plus bonuses. Keep that amendment distinct from the unamended printed table; do not infer an unconditional natural-20 rule from it.

comparisonExamples.explanation: With no additional adjustments in this illustration, the original matrix's repeated 20 differs from the linear calculation 20 − (−1).
The source-listed cell is 20; a simple AC-zero subtraction would produce 24. No missing cells were generated from that formula.

coverage.label: All 210 attack matrix cells visually checked against the supplied scan.
coverage.method: The 210 cells were read against printed DMG page 74 and independently compared; this check is limited to the matrix cells.
coverage.missingCellsMeaning: A null indicates an unavailable value; it never means an impossible hit or a target score of zero.

cellVerification.scope: 210 attack matrix cells only; other combat mechanics and notes retain their own review status.
